data.name: Lost in Paradise
data.detailed_description:
----- Tradução profissional -----

Mergulhe num paraíso perdido, com um grande mistério que se esconde além de suas fronteiras primitivas.



Membro da tripulação de um barco que naufragou súbita e misteriosamente em sua passagem pelo Triângulo das Bermudas, você é o único sobrevivente numa ilha aparentemente deserta. Deserta mas nem sempre desabitada. Solucione o mistério do paraíso perdido e reivindique a sua sorte. Volte-se para a natureza, aprenda e refine suas habilidades de sobrevivência no mundo REAL, resolva enigmas e viva a aventura.

Perdido no Paraíso é uma aventura em terceira pessoa no estilo de apontar e clicar que lembra os jogos clássicos dos anos 90 (semelhante a jogos de fuga modernos, porém mais aprofundado) com gráficos fascinantes, animação e um estilo de arte exclusivo.

  • Explore mais de 25 lugares naturais e surpreendentes com animações vivas e brilhantes, sons e efeitos climáticos.
  • Curta seis lindas trilhas sonoras com músicas misteriosas e relaxantes feitas especialmente para a ambientação e os enigmas (com controle de volume interno)
  • Mais de uma dúzia de enigmas lógicos e mini jogos para desafiá-lo, mexer com seu cérebro e testar suas habilidades.
  • Aprenda verdadeiras técnicas de sobrevivência que você poderá usar no mundo real, como montar um acampamento, fazer uma faca, corda e muito mais no meio ambiente selvagem.
  • Ajunte pistas, anotações e outros itens para solucionar charadas e esclarecer o mistério da ilha.
  • Mapa do jogo para viajar facilmente entre os locais e diário do jogo para registrar e guardar as pistas.
  • Sistema tutorial do jogo para jogadores iniciantes. Caso você seja um jogador ocasional ou habitual, o jogo é bom para todos.
  • Contexto sensitivo de dicas — Se você estiver com problemas, pode obter uma única dica naquela hora, para ir adiante, sem ter que deixar o jogo e rever todas as instruções e destaques.
  • Sistema de destaque local — nenhum caça pixel é tudo "gameplay".
  • Suporte multilíngue — atualmente disponível em Português, Inglês, Alemão, Francês, Espanhol, Italiano,, sueco, coreano, japonês, russo e hindi.

reviews.review:
Lost in Paradise is a traditional point-and-click adventure built around exploration, puzzle solving, and a mysterious survival story. Developed and published by Elev8 Games, it begins with a voyage through the Bermuda Triangle that goes disastrously wrong when the protagonist's ship capsizes. Waking up on an unfamiliar tropical island with no obvious means of escape provides an immediately understandable objective: survive, explore the surroundings, and determine what actually happened. The island soon proves to be more mysterious than an ordinary deserted paradise, giving the adventure a sense of uncertainty that encourages players to keep investigating.

Rather than functioning as a demanding survival simulator, the game uses survival concepts as the foundation for its puzzles. Players explore more than 25 locations while collecting objects, examining points of interest, discovering clues, and solving problems that gradually open additional possibilities. Some challenges incorporate practical ideas such as starting a fire, making rope, and constructing simple tools. These activities are presented through accessible adventure-game mechanics instead of complicated crafting systems. This makes the survival theme approachable while giving many of the puzzles a logical connection to the protagonist's circumstances.

The game contains more than a dozen logic puzzles and mini-games, and their variety helps prevent the journey from becoming entirely dependent on conventional inventory combinations. Observation and experimentation are important, but Lost in Paradise also provides several features designed to reduce the frustration historically associated with older point-and-click adventures. Different difficulty settings allow players to adjust the challenge, while a context-sensitive hint system can provide assistance when a solution becomes difficult to determine. The hints are especially useful because they can offer guidance without necessarily giving away the complete answer immediately.

Another welcome convenience is the ability to highlight interactive hotspots. Older adventure games sometimes require players to scan every small portion of the screen looking for a barely visible object, but this feature makes it easier to identify meaningful areas. A tutorial explains the basic systems, making the experience suitable even for players without extensive familiarity with the genre. These accessibility features do reduce some of the old-fashioned difficulty, but they generally improve the pacing by allowing the player to concentrate on reasoning rather than pixel hunting.

Exploring the island remains an important part of the experience. The environments include tropical scenery accompanied by animated elements, environmental sounds, weather effects, and music associated with different locations and puzzles. The graphical presentation is clearly modest and shows the limitations of a smaller, older production, but the natural setting works well for the premise. Peaceful scenery occasionally contrasts effectively with the protagonist's isolation and the unanswered questions surrounding the island. The result is an atmosphere that can feel relaxing during exploration while retaining an underlying sense that something unusual is waiting to be discovered.

Navigation is made considerably easier through an in-game map, which is useful when previously explored areas need to be revisited. The diary performs a similarly practical role by recording important clues and information. These systems are particularly valuable because point-and-click adventures frequently expect players to remember discoveries made much earlier. Instead of requiring extensive handwritten notes, the game keeps much of the necessary information accessible. Steam Cloud support and achievements are also available, alongside additional Steam-oriented features such as trading cards, statistics, and leaderboards.

The story is relatively straightforward in presentation and mainly exists to give context to the exploration and puzzles. The Bermuda Triangle provides an appropriate backdrop for unexplained events, and the player gradually discovers information through environmental investigation, notes, objects, and clues. Those expecting a cinematic narrative filled with elaborate dialogue and complex character development may find the storytelling restrained. The appeal instead comes from uncovering the island's secrets piece by piece and allowing curiosity to drive progress.

Lost in Paradise works best when treated as a compact adventure game rather than a full-scale survival experience. Its survival lessons are interesting and help distinguish it from more conventional point-and-click titles, but they are intentionally simplified. Likewise, players looking for combat, extensive crafting, open-world resource management, or highly sophisticated simulation systems will not find those elements here. The experience favors careful observation, logical thinking, exploration, and relatively relaxed progression.

Steam Deck compatibility is less certain. The game does not have a prominent official Steam Deck compatibility rating confirming it as Verified or Playable. Given its older PC-focused point-and-click design, players should consider its Steam Deck status officially unverified rather than assume complete compatibility. It may be possible to run it through SteamOS and Proton, but interface behavior, text readability, controls, video playback, or other technical details could require adjustments. Using the touchscreen, trackpads, or a custom controller layout may also be preferable to standard gamepad controls because the original interface was designed around mouse interaction.

Overall, Lost in Paradise is an interesting example of a smaller adventure game using an isolated tropical setting to combine traditional puzzle mechanics with basic survival concepts. Its visual presentation is dated and its individual systems are not especially deep, but the accessible hints, hotspot highlighting, map, diary, multiple difficulty options, varied puzzles, and unusual survival theme give it personality. Players nostalgic for classic point-and-click adventures are likely to appreciate its deliberate pace more than those seeking modern action or sophisticated survival mechanics. Despite its limitations, it provides a pleasantly unusual journey for puzzle fans willing to explore its mysterious island.

Rating: 6/10
